failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs did well here: `Which processor should I use?` steers DOM-style text extraction to `WP_HTML_Processor`; `Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree` gives the exact `create_fragment()` + `next_tag()` + depth-bounded `next_token()` + `#text` + `get_modifiable_text()` pattern; `get_current_depth()` explains why the subtree guard must use `>=`; `next_token()` explains that it does not stop at the earlier matched element and that malformed/unclosed elements still produce structural closers; and `get_modifiable_text()` clearly states decoded text semantics. The only near-misses are low-priority: examples sometimes rely on surrounding prose for `create_fragment()` null handling, and the incomplete-input policy is spread across several sections rather than summarized next to the subtree text recipe.

doc_gaps.problem: The method docs say `create_fragment()` can return `null`, but several examples proceed directly to `next_tag()`. Less careful readers may copy the examples without a guard.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note to examples that omit the guard, or include the null check in the canonical text-walk example.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain incomplete input and virtual closers, but the read-only extraction policy is distributed across the recipe, `next_token()`, and `get_current_depth()`.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one compact sentence to the subtree text recipe: read-only extraction may return accumulated text after virtual end-of-input closure when that matches the caller contract; mutations or complete-source contracts should check `paused_at_incomplete_token()` and `get_last_error()`.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs correctly warn that modifiable text is not a predicate, but this is an easy API trap because empty string can mean either no modifiable text or genuinely empty text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small do/don't snippet showing `get_token_type() === '#text'` as the predicate and avoiding truthiness checks on `get_modifiable_text()`.
